articles.title: NASA Demonstrates Next-Generation Heat Shield Technologies
articles.description: NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24th cargo resupply mission for NASA undocked from the International Space Station, it carried a fleet of 12 small, experimental capsules designed to […]
articles.summary: NASA successfully tests advanced heat shield technologies designed to protect astronauts during Moon and Mars return missions. These innovations represent major progress toward safe deep-space exploration.

articles.title: Largest 2D map of the universe helps scientists discover new gravitational lenses
articles.description: Using data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, with help from artificial intelligence, an international team of scientists has discovered 70 new gravitational lenses—rare cosmic alignments that act as natural magnifying glasses. The new lenses further expand one of the largest collections of confirmed lenses to date and will allow scientists to study dark matter, galaxy evolution and the structure of the universe.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: An international team using DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys data and artificial intelligence has created the largest 2D map of the universe, enabling the discovery of new gravitational lenses. This breakthrough enhances our understanding of cosmic structure and dark matter distribution.

articles.title: Researchers May Have Directly Glimpsed an Exoplanet’s Magnetic Field for the First Time, Building Hope of Peering Deeper Into Faraway Worlds
articles.description: Radio signals emanating from Beta Pictoris b suggest that this young and massive exoplanet has a strong magnetic field and intense auroral show
articles.summary: Researchers have potentially detected an exoplanet's magnetic field for the first time through radio signals from Beta Pictoris b, opening new avenues for understanding distant worlds. This landmark discovery suggests young, massive exoplanets possess stronger magnetic fields than previously theorized.

articles.title: Francis Halzen Wins Nobel Physics Prize For Antarctic 'Ghost Particle' Hunt
articles.description: University of Wisconsin-Madison physicist Francis Halzen has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his contributions to understanding astrophysical neutrinos. Halzen led the development of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory beneath the Antarctic ice,…
articles.summary: Physicist Francis Halzen wins the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his pioneering work on the IceCube neutrino observatory in Antarctica. This recognition celebrates a transformative breakthrough in detecting high-energy cosmic particles from the universe's most violent events.

articles.summary: Scientists use ice-based detectors to capture and study cosmic neutrinos from distant cosmic events. This innovative approach reveals fundamental insights about the universe's highest-energy phenomena.

articles.title: NASA Seeks US Industry Plans for Commercial Space Stations
articles.description: NASA is advancing American leadership in space by taking the next step toward a future where commercial space stations lead the way in low Earth orbit. On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations. “In alignment with the President’s National […]
articles.summary: NASA partners with US commercial industry to develop next-generation space stations in low Earth orbit. This initiative accelerates private space infrastructure and enables expanded research opportunities.

articles.title: Cosmic House of Mirrors
articles.description: Galaxies warp and multiply as if in a house of mirrors in this image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Sept. 29, 2026. The brilliant golden galaxies seen here are part of a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies bunched together on one side of the image, however, are not actually […]
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures stunning gravitational lensing phenomena where galaxy light bends and multiplies around massive cosmic structures. This reveals the universe's hidden mass and structure.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The ESA's Solar Orbiter mission solves the mystery of magnetic switchbacks—S-shaped kinks in the solar wind near the Sun. This breakthrough advances understanding of solar dynamics and space weather.

articles.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
articles.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express, in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.
articles.summary: The ESA's Mars Express reveals surprising new details about Mars's unusual atmospheric clouds using advanced meteorological modeling. These discoveries deepen our understanding of Martian atmospheric science.

articles.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.description:
Image:
			Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures dynamic stellar jets erupting from nebulae, revealing the violent energy release during star formation. These images showcase the cosmos's most dramatic creative processes.

articles.title: Science begins for Smile
articles.description: On 23 September, the European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready to start revealing how Earth responds to the wind of charged particles from the Sun. This follows a busy in-space commissioning period since the spacecraft launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit for science operations on 20 June.
articles.summary: The European-Chinese Smile mission begins its scientific operations to study how Earth's magnetosphere responds to solar wind interactions. This collaborative mission opens new perspectives on space weather dynamics.

articles.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
articles.description:
Image:
			
This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us.
MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the Universe was about 8 billion years old. While this galaxy cluster is a valuable scientific target in its own right, the real stars of this image are the galaxies that appear warped and stretched, like a painting that has been smeared by a giant hand.
The way these galaxies look is the result of gravitational lensing, in which the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Gravitational lensing allows astronomers to observe galaxies, star clusters and even individual stars that are too far away for our telescopes to see under normal conditions. While the large, orange galaxies appear obviously distorted, look carefully at some of the small reddish background galaxies throughout this picture: even at the very edges of the frame, there are galaxies whose images have been bent into tiny arcs by MACS J0454.1-0300’s gravity.
The gravitationally lensed areas show multiple images of galaxies from when the Universe was young: a group of galaxies 2 billion years after the Big Bang, and a single galaxy just 800 million years old after the Big Bang. The galaxy group appears to be going through a merger, resulting in an enormous burst of star formation.
Astronomers have also identified individual bright ‘knots’ within the gravitationally lensed areas, corresponding to regions as small as 5 light-years across. These tiny clumps appear magnified by a factor of more than 300, in some cases.
A NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image of this same cluster was released in 2014. Take a moment to compare the two images; the difference between them is dramatic. The new Webb image reveals hundreds of galaxies missing from the earlier image. These galaxies were there all along, but Webb is much more sensitive to their much redder light.
The data behind this image come from two observing programmes (#5058, PI: Furtak; #6882, PI: Fujimoto) that leverage the ability of massive galaxy clusters to bring distant objects into view.
[Image Description: A massive galaxy cluster, made of many golden elliptical galaxies with the largest, brightest one in the centre. Heavily distorted orange galaxies appear all around the cluster, the largest concentrated in a large arc around the cluster's centre; these are images of very distant galaxies, created by gravitational lensing. A few galaxies are large and bluish-white in colour; bright, nearby stars are the same colour.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope's Picture of the Month reveals distant galaxies with unprecedented detail through gravitational lensing effects. This composite view unveils the universe's earliest galaxies and cosmic structure.

articles.title: Successful Earth flyby improves Juice’s course to Jupiter
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) skimmed the very outer edge of Earth’s atmosphere on 28 September, using the gravity of our home planet to alter its route to Jupiter using very little fuel.
articles.summary: The ESA's Juice spacecraft successfully executes an Earth gravity assist flyby to refine its trajectory toward Jupiter and its icy moons. This maneuver represents critical progress toward one of humanity's most ambitious exploration missions.

articles.title: The Preliminary Lunar Science Report for Artemis II is Out!
articles.description: Through photographs, spoken observations, drawings, and annotations, the Artemis II crew created a unique scientific record—one that is now available to the science community and the public for further study. Explore highlights here, and find the full suite of reports and select data resources at the bottom of the page.
articles.summary: The Artemis II preliminary lunar science report documents groundbreaking observations and discoveries made during the historic crewed lunar mission.

articles.title: Astronomers Detect Potential ‘Second Generation’ Planet Around Dying Stellar White Dwarf
articles.description: Potential ‘Second generation’ planet detection around a dying stellar white dwarf opens a whole new chapter of exoplanetary science.
articles.summary: Astronomers have detected a potential second-generation planet orbiting a white dwarf star, opening new possibilities for understanding planetary survival and formation.

articles.title: The Most Distant FRB Tells The Story Of Its Origin
articles.description: Astronomers use the Webb to study a distant fast radio burst and reveal clues as to the origin of these mysterious events.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope studies the most distant fast radio burst detected, revealing clues about the mysterious origins of these cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Webb Observes "Extreme Debris Disks," Providing a Window into the Early Solar System
articles.description: In the early history of our solar system, scientists theorize that a Mars-sized object called Theia smashed into the infant Earth, creating the Earth-Moon system. Using Webb, astronomers are studying young star systems to learn more about the early Solar System's evolution.
articles.summary: Webb observations of extreme debris disks provide crucial insights into the violent early history of our solar system and planetary formation.

articles.title: Discovery marks the first detection of variable water clouds outside of the solar system
articles.description: A Jupiter-sized world just 7.5 light-years away is cloudy, chemically complex and, it turns out, more like home than anyone expected. Using the James Webb Space Telescope, Brittany Miles, assistant astronomer at the University of Arizona's Steward Observatory, led a team that spent 11 hours staring at WISE 0855, the coldest known brown dwarf, collecting a spectrum of its light every 15 minutes.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers discover the first variable water clouds outside our solar system on a nearby Jupiter-sized world, revealing Earth-like atmospheric chemistry.

articles.title: Astronomers pinpoint the most distant fast radio burst ever detected
articles.description: Astronomers have detected and traced the most distant fast radio burst ever recorded, a powerful flash of radio waves that traveled for more than 10 billion years across the cosmos before reaching Earth.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers detect and locate the most distant fast radio burst ever recorded, pushing the boundaries of cosmic observation.

articles.title: NASA astronauts splash down after 100 million miles in space
articles.description: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 astronauts have returned to Earth after 237 days in space, traveling more than 100 million miles and completing over 3,792 orbits while conducting research to prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars. The mission also made history with record-setting spacewalk achievements and experiments that could transform medicine both in space and on Earth.
articles.summary: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 astronauts have successfully returned to Earth after 237 days in orbit, completing a landmark mission traveling over 100 million miles. This achievement demonstrates the continued success of commercial-government partnerships in human spaceflight.

articles.title: NASA is searching for hidden caves to build its first Moon base
articles.description: NASA is preparing for humanity’s first Moon base with three investigations that will hunt for underground shelters, uncover hidden ice, and track dangerous conditions on the lunar surface. The findings could reveal how astronauts can survive and thrive on the Moon while laying the groundwork for future journeys to Mars.
articles.summary: NASA is investigating underground caves and shelters on the Moon to prepare for humanity's first permanent lunar base. These three investigations will identify safe, protected locations for future lunar habitation.

articles.title: MIT astronomers catch a star in a feast that could last billions of years
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered a bizarre star system about 300 light-years from Earth where a small star is slowly devouring a nearby brown dwarf, an object too massive to be a planet but too small to be a true star. Unlike stars that rapidly swallow their companions, this one is gradually stealing material in a process that could continue for billions of years.
articles.summary: MIT astronomers have discovered a remarkable binary star system 300 light-years away where a small star is slowly devouring its companion over billions of years. This rare astronomical phenomenon provides insights into stellar evolution and mass transfer processes.

articles.title: NASA’s Webb finds signs of Mars-sized worlds smashing together
articles.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope is giving astronomers a glimpse of the kinds of violent collisions that may have shaped our own solar system, including the giant impact thought to have created the Moon. By studying 21 rare “extreme debris disks” around young stars, researchers found that their dust can reveal the scale and intensity of planetary collisions.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has observed evidence of Mars-sized planetary collisions in distant star systems, revealing the violent processes that may have shaped planetary formation. These observations illuminate how planetary systems develop and evolve.

articles.title: A 9-billion-year-old signal could help explain dark energy
articles.description: A Canadian radio telescope has detected the faint glow of hydrogen from billions of years ago using only its own observations, proving a long-awaited way to map the distant universe can actually work. CHIME can use this hydrogen signal to trace how matter is spread across space and measure how the universe has expanded over time, offering a powerful new way to investigate dark energy.
articles.summary: A Canadian radio telescope has detected a 9-billion-year-old hydrogen signal using innovative detection methods, providing new data to help explain dark energy. This discovery offers fresh perspectives on cosmic expansion and the universe's largest-scale structure.

articles.title: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot returns from her first mission to the International Space Station
articles.description: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot has arrived back in Europe, landing in Cologne, Germany, following her return to Earth with Crew-12 after 237 days, nearly eight months, aboard the International Space Station for her εpsilon mission.
articles.summary: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot has successfully returned to Europe after completing her first mission aboard the International Space Station. Her 235-day expedition represents another triumph in international space collaboration and human spaceflight.

articles.title: Doomed NASA spacecraft beams back stunning cosmic images weeks before fiery plunge to Earth
articles.description: A doomed spacecraft set to plunge to Earth in weeks has shared new cosmic images.
articles.summary: A NASA spacecraft continues to capture breathtaking cosmic imagery during its final weeks before completing its mission. The spacecraft's remarkable observations expand our understanding of the universe even as it completes its operational lifecycle.

articles.title: Nasa struggled to sample Bennu until Brian May revealed its hidden dangers
articles.description: A rock musician working at a computer might seem an unlikely figure in an asteroid-sampling mission, but Brian May brought a specialist skill to Nasa’s
articles.summary: Musician and astrophysicist Brian May provided crucial insights that helped NASA overcome sampling challenges during the Bennu asteroid collection mission. His interdisciplinary contributions highlight how diverse expertise drives scientific discovery.

articles.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day highlights Stickney Crater on Mars's moon Phobos, showcasing the dramatic geology of the Martian system. This celestial landmark offers clues to the moon's violent history.

articles.title: Happy New Year on Mars
articles.description: 30 September 2026 marks the start of a new year on Mars. At exactly 10:16 CEST/08:16 UTC on Earth, the Red Planet begins a new orbit around our Sun.
articles.summary: Mars celebrates the arrival of its new year, marking the start of another chapter in planetary timekeeping and ongoing exploration. This milestone underscores humanity's continuous presence on and study of the Red Planet.
